#2204. Calciomercato no stop - Indiscrezioni, trattative e retroscena del 3 novembre

INTER, ALL'OPERA PER I RINNOVI DI DIMARCO, CALHANOGLU E THURAM. JUVENTUS, IL RETROSCENA DI GREGORIO-MANDAS. LAZIO, SIRENE DALLA PREMIER LEAGUE PER TAYLOR. FROSINONE, PRONTO A QUINTUPLICARE L'INGAGGIO DI KVERNADZE. SASSUOLO, LIPANI RINNOVA E PER LAURIENTÈ NON MANCANO GLI ESTIMATORI IN INGHILTERRA

BOLOGNA Il Bologna guarda al futuro e monitora con interesse la crescita di Motiejus Sapola, difensore centrale lituano classe 2006 di proprietà del Pisa, attualmente in prestito allo Spezia, capolista imbattuto del Girone B di Serie C. Le prestazioni del giovane, che potrebbe anche ricevere la convocazione della nazionale maggiore per gli impegni di Nations League di novembre, hanno attirato l'attenzione di diversi club di categoria superiore. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Secolo XIX, oltre al Frosinone anche il Bologna segue il centrale in vista della stagione 2027/28, individuato come un possibile rinforzo giovane e fisicamente strutturato per la retroguardia. Il Pisa, che crede nelle qualità del giocatore, ha fissato un riscatto a 800 mila euro, mantenendo un diritto di controriscatto a 200 mila: cifre che potrebbero però aumentare qualora l'interesse della Serie A diventasse più concreto.

FROSINONE Il Frosinone lavora su più fronti, tra il presente e le prospettive del mercato. La priorità riguarda Giorgi Kvernadze, protagonista di un ottimo avvio di stagione con tre gol e quattro assist in dieci giornate: il club di Stirpe è pronto a proporgli un rinnovo fino a circa un milione di euro a stagione, cinque volte l'attuale ingaggio, per blindarlo ed evitare che possa finire sul mercato già a gennaio, considerando il contratto in scadenza nel 2028 e l'interesse di diverse società. Intanto emerge un retroscena di mercato su Gustavo Varela, oggi al Monza e capocannoniere della Serie B con nove reti: la scorsa estate il Frosinone aveva raggiunto un accordo con il Benfica per acquistarlo a 2,5 milioni di euro, con il 50% sulla futura rivendita, salvo poi scegliere Tomas Bobcek, arrivato dal Lechia Danzica per 11 milioni. Sul fronte delle possibili uscite, invece, Francesco Gelli potrebbe lasciare i ciociari a gennaio dopo essere finito ai margini della prima squadra: sulle sue tracce c'è lo Spezia di Guido Angelozzi, che lo aveva portato in giallazzurro nel 2023. Infine, proprio lo Spezia potrebbe rappresentare un'opportunità anche per il futuro: il club ligure, attraverso il lavoro di Angelozzi, segue Motiejus Sapola, difensore classe 2006 di proprietà del Pisa, che interessa anche al Bologna in vista della stagione 2027/28.

INTER L'Inter è al lavoro su più fronti per definire il futuro della propria rosa, con diversi dossier contrattuali aperti. Per Federico Dimarco, dopo l'esercizio dell'opzione fino al 2028, sono previsti nei prossimi giorni contatti con i nuovi agenti per discutere un adeguamento dell'ingaggio e un prolungamento a lungo termine, con la volontà comune di proseguire insieme. Procede spedita anche la trattativa per il rinnovo di Carlos Augusto, mentre per Marcus Thuram ogni discorso è rimandato a un secondo momento. Più delicata la situazione di Hakan Çalhanoğlu, in scadenza a giugno e senza opzioni automatiche: il turco vorrebbe un biennale per restare a Milano, ma sullo sfondo ci sono interessamenti dalla Turchia e altre possibili destinazioni. Sul fronte del mercato, invece, torna d'attualità il nome di Lisandro Martinez: il Manchester United starebbe valutando una possibile cessione a gennaio e l'Inter, insieme a Roma e Como, osserva con attenzione gli sviluppi, considerando l'opportunità di riportare in Serie A il centrale argentino. Infine, uno sguardo al futuro delle corsie esterne: piace nuovamente Givairo Read, talento classe 2006 del Feyenoord già seguito in estate dopo l'addio di Dumfries. Il club olandese aveva respinto anche un'offerta della Roma da circa 30 milioni di euro, ma il rendimento del giovane esterno, autore di sei assist in undici gare di Eredivisie, continua a convincere.

JUVENTUS La vittoria contro il Napoli rappresenta un primo passo importante nel percorso di ripartenza della Juventus, ma la dirigenza è consapevole che restano diverse situazioni da sistemare e guarda già al mercato di gennaio. La priorità è un terzino sinistro che possa affiancare Andrea Cambiaso: sul taccuino ci sono David Raum del Lipsia, Rayan Ait-Nouri del Manchester City e Mahamadou Nagida del Rennes. Attenzione anche al centrocampo, dove Teun Koopmeiners non è considerato incedibile e tra i profili valutati spicca Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg del Marsiglia. Si ragiona inoltre su un possibile intervento in attacco: tra i nomi accostati ai bianconeri figurano Folarin Balogun, Alexander Sorloth e Mauro Icardi, ma un eventuale acquisto richiederebbe anche una cessione, con Edon Zhegrova tra i possibili partenti. Intanto emerge un retroscena della scorsa estate: la Juventus aveva valutato seriamente Christos Mandas, portiere della Lazio protagonista di un ottimo avvio di stagione con quattro clean sheet in undici presenze, prendendo in considerazione anche uno scambio con Michele Di Gregorio. L'operazione non si concretizzò per la volontà di Gennaro Gattuso di puntare sul greco, il cui valore oggi viene stimato tra i 20 e i 25 milioni di euro. Sul fronte dei giovani, infine, arriva una notizia ufficiale: Destiny Elimoghale, esterno offensivo classe 2009 già aggregato alla Juventus Next Gen, ha rinnovato il contratto fino al 30 giugno 2029, confermando la volontà del club di investire sul suo percorso di crescita.

LAZIO La Lazio si gode il primato in classifica e lavora contemporaneamente per blindare i suoi protagonisti. Tra questi c'è Kenneth Taylor, centrocampista olandese arrivato dall'Ajax nel gennaio 2026 per un'operazione da 17 milioni di euro bonus compresi, che ha già attirato l'interesse della Premier League: Brighton e Bournemouth hanno effettuato i primi sondaggi dopo un avvio di stagione da due gol e due assist in dieci presenze. La società biancoceleste non ha intenzione di privarsene a gennaio, ma dovrà prestare attenzione ai possibili sviluppi in vista dell'estate. Intanto sono iniziati i contatti per il rinnovo di Gustav Isaksen, il cui contratto scade nel 2028: l'obiettivo è prolungare almeno fino al 2030, accompagnando l'accordo con un adeguamento economico, dopo la crescita dell'esterno danese, già autore di quattro reti in dieci giornate. Tra le note più positive c'è anche Christos Mandas, protagonista di un ottimo rendimento con quattro clean sheet in undici presenze e dieci gol subiti. Il portiere greco, acquistato dall'OFI Creta per appena 951mila euro, oggi ha una valutazione stimata tra i 20 e i 25 milioni. La scorsa estate la Juventus aveva provato a inserirlo in un possibile scambio con Michele Di Gregorio, ma Gennaro Gattuso ha voluto trattenerlo a Roma, puntando su di lui come titolare: una scelta che sta dando ampiamente ragione all'allenatore.

MONZA Il Monza si gode l'esplosione di Gustavo Varela, attaccante portoghese arrivato in estate dal Benfica e attualmente capocannoniere della Serie B con nove reti in dieci presenze, una in più rispetto ad Antonio Raimondo, ora costretto a fermarsi per qualche settimana a causa di un infortunio. Intanto emerge un retroscena di mercato raccolto da Tuttomercatoweb.com: la scorsa estate Varela era stato molto vicino al Frosinone, che aveva raggiunto un accordo con il Benfica per acquistarlo a 2,5 milioni di euro, lasciando al club portoghese il 50% sulla futura rivendita. I ciociari avevano però successivamente scelto di puntare su Tomas Bobcek, arrivato dal Lechia Danzica per 11 milioni. A quel punto si è inserito il Monza, che ha chiuso l'operazione per circa 2 milioni più bonus, riconoscendo al Benfica il 20% sulla futura rivendita e un diritto di prelazione: in caso di un'offerta ufficiale da parte di un altro club, i lusitani potranno infatti pareggiarla e riportare il giocatore in patria.

SASSUOLO Il Sassuolo guarda al futuro e blinda Luca Lipani: il centrocampista classe 2005 ha firmato un rinnovo quinquennale che lo legherà al club neroverde fino al 30 giugno 2031, confermando la volontà della società di puntare sui giovani talenti nonostante il difficile avvio di stagione. Intanto resta aperto il capitolo Armand Laurienté, ancora uno dei principali uomini mercato della formazione emiliana. L'esterno francese, sotto contratto fino al 2029, continua a essere seguito in Italia e all'estero: in estate si erano mosse l'Ipswich Town e diverse società turche, tra cui Fenerbahce, Besiktas e Trabzonspor, senza però raggiungere la valutazione di almeno 25 milioni di euro fissata dal Sassuolo. Anche il Napoli potrebbe tornare a interessarsi al giocatore, già inserito nella propria lista durante la scorsa sessione invernale. La posizione ufficiale del club, attraverso il ds Francesco Palmieri, è quella di non voler cedere i propri giocatori a gennaio, ma l'interesse per Laurienté potrebbe comunque riaccendere le trattative in vista del mercato invernale.

FONSECA È TORNATO IN PORTOGALLO: ADDIO LIONE, QUESTIONE DI ORE L'ANNUNCIO CON LO SPORTING LISBONA. FABIO CANNAVARO PUO' LASCIARE LA PANCHINA DELL'UZBEKISTAN. COSA SUCCEDE AL FENERBAHCE: SERGIO CONCEICAO NON ARRIVA. NUNO ESPIRITO SANTO ESONERATO DAL WEST HAM.

Paulo Fonseca è sbarcato all'aeroporto Humberto Delgado di Lisbona per formalizzare il suo passaggio allo Sporting, pronto a raccogliere l'eredità di Rui Borges ad Alvalade dopo aver risolto gli ultimi dettagli contrattuali per l'addio al Lione. L'ex tecnico del Milan, che ha salutato tra le lacrime i gones al termine della vittoria per 2-0 sull'Angers in Ligue 1, ha espresso la propria felicità per il ritorno in patria, rimandando ogni approfondimento ai prossimi giorni. Nella giornata di mercoledì, con il rientro dall'Inghilterra del presidente del club lusitano Frederico Varandas, si procederà alla firma del contratto che legherà il cinquantatreenne alla società lusitana fino al 2030 con un ingaggio da 3 milioni di euro netti a stagione, mentre nelle casse dell'OL andrà un indennizzo pari a 5 milioni di euro per liberare l'allenatore.

Si appresta a vivere uno snodo cruciale l'esperienza di Fabio Cannavaro alla guida dell'Uzbekistan, con l'ex Pallone d'oro pronto a rassegnare le dimissioni da commissario tecnico a causa del rinvio di quasi un anno della Coppa d'Asia 2027, come svelato da Fabrizio Romano. Subentrato nell'ottobre 2025 a Timur Kapadze - l'uomo che aveva condotto la selezione al suo primo storico pass per i Mondiali 2026 -, l'ex difensore di Inter e Juventus ha subito avvertito il peso della responsabilità, assumendosi la paternità dell'eliminazione rimediata la scorsa estate con tre sconfitte nella fase a gironi del torneo iridato, pur rimarcando la crescita maturata dalla squadra su scala globale. Resta ora da capire se sarà ancora lui a dirigere gli uzbeki nei test internazionali programmati per il mese di novembre contro Russia e Arabia Saudita.

Fumata nera in casa Fenerbahce per l'approdo in panchina di Sergio Conceiçao. Nonostante l'intesa totale non fosse ancora stata raggiunta, la trattativa sembrava incanalata verso la fumata bianca, ma il tavolo negoziale è saltato improvvisamente nella notte: il club di Istanbul ha giudicato eccessive le pretese salariali avanzate dall'ex allenatore del Milan, scegliendo di virare con decisione su un profilo autoctono. Nel mirino dei gialloblù è così finito Emre Belozoglu, autentica bandiera della società con tre differenti parentesi da calciatore (2008-12, 2013-15 e 2019/20) e un'esperienza da tecnico avviata proprio al Fener nel 2021 dopo l'esonero di Erol Bulut. L'operazione per riportare a casa l'ex centrocampista dell'Inter presenta tuttavia un ostacolo di mercato: Emre è attualmente vincolato al Kasimpasa - quinto in classifica a quota 17 punti dopo 10 giornate -, costringendo il Fenerbahçe a trattare la liberazione del tecnico dietro il pagamento di un indennizzo ai rivali di campionato.

Termina l'esperienza di Nuno Espirito Santo sulla panchina del West Ham. Il tecnico portoghese, alla guida del club londinese dal settembre del 2025, è stato esonerato dal club dopo la brutta partenza in Championship (la seconda divisione inglese) con l'ottavo posto e appena 22 punti conquistati in 13 presenze. Il West Ham United conferma che l'allenatore della prima squadra maschile, Nuno Espírito Santo, ha lasciato il suo incarico con effetto immediato. A seguito di un'attenta analisi dell'inizio di stagione dell'EFL Championship, il Consiglio di Amministrazione ritiene necessario un cambiamento per garantire che gli obiettivi del Club rimangano in linea con le aspettative. Anche l'assistente allenatore Rui Pedro Silva e l'allenatore dei portieri Rui Barbosa hanno lasciato lo staff. Il West Ham United desidera ringraziare Nuno, Rui e Rui per il loro impegno e la dedizione dimostrati durante la loro permanenza nel Club, e augura loro tutto il meglio per il futuro.

#2203. Harry Redknapp says 46-year-old will be a ‘great fit’ for West Ham as managerial appointment nears

West Ham are expected to turn to their former player as their new head coach following their decision to part ways with Nuno Espirito Santo. WHUFC are positioned in 8th place in the Championship table after their first 13 fixtures of the season as they eye promotion back to the Premier League.

Parker, 46, cut ties with Burnley in late April and is available for work. He has been weighing up his options over the last six months.

Redknapp, who both played for and managed the Hammers, has delivered his verdict on talkSPORT: “Scott’s got a great record in the Championship and has taken teams up. He knows the club. He was a very, very good player. I took him from West Ham to Tottenham. Good lad. He’s a very astute manager. I think he’s a great fit for West Ham.”

He added: “He hasn’t got an easy job on his hands. Take (Jarrod) Bowen apart, there’s very few players there who would have got into too many West Ham teams over the years. They’ve got great support, it’s a big club that unfortunately needs a big lift now.”

Parker played 129 games for West Ham during his playing days. As well as WHUFC, he also had spells at Charlton Athletic, Chelsea, Newcastle United, Tottenham Hotspur and Fulham.

The ex-England international, who made 18 caps for his country, hung up his boots in 2017. He has since delved into the managerial world.

He started coaching at Spurs before returning to Fulham as their manager in 2019. He guided the Whites to promotion to the Premier League in 2020 before doing the same with AFC Bournemouth two years later.

The London-born man also got Burnley up in 2025 so he knows what it takes to get out of the EFL. He has also managed abroad following a stint at Club Brugge in Belgium before his switch to Turf Moor.

As Redknapp has alluded to, Parker has promotion experience and knows West Ham well already. He should be able to get the WHUFC fans onside.

The Hammers need to find some form as they look to claw themselves back into the top flight at the first time of asking. They are in the top eight along with Wolves, West Brom, Southampton, Birmingham City and Stoke City as they chase down the top two Middlesbrough and Swansea City.

They lost 3-1 at home against West Brom last time out and were poor against the Baggies. They are back in action on Wednesday night with an away trip to South Wales to take on Cardiff City as they aim to get themselves back on track and return to winning ways.

West Ham managed to keep hold of Jarrod Bowen in the last transfer window. He has been prolific so far this term but needs some of his teammates to step up now.

The London outfit will get the chance to bolster their ranks this winter. They will also have the opportunity to let some players head out the exit door as well in January.

#2202. James Penrice expecting '10 times’ the joy if Rangers lift Premier Sports Cup

James Penrice enjoyed Rangers’ Premier Sports Cup semi-final victory over Aberdeen but believes the winning feeling will multiply by 10 if they win the final.

The Light Blues registered a 1-0 victory at Barclays Hampden on Saturday thanks to a late but deserved goal from striker Ryan Naderi, who pounced on a strike towards goal from Penrice to direct the ball into the net from six yards.

Gers players took the acclaim of their fans at the end after confirming Derek McInnes’ first final as boss, with Rangers facing Hibernian at the national stadium on December 13 after the Hibees beat city rivals Hearts 2-1 on Sunday.

Penrice, on loan from Super League Greece side AEK Athens, said: “I think it’s special seeing boys that haven’t seen the kind of scenes before, haven’t seen Rangers at Hampden.

“I think it can only help. And I think it will be 10 times that if you were to come back here and win it in six weeks.

“So the motivation for the boys is to relive that again, 10 times that.

“And I think that’s what we’ll be trying to put into the group and it can only help us.”

Penrice admits his decision to join the Ibrox side in the summer was vindicated – albeit there had been no hesitation.

The former Partick Thistle, Livingston and Hearts left-back said: “It was never in doubt. Never.

“It was the only place I wanted to go in the summer. And I pushed a hell of a lot.

“This is why I want to come here and play for a massive club and play in games like a final. It only backs up my decision.”

It was not a classic display from Rangers, especially in a low-quality first half but Penrice stressed the importance of digging deep to get results.

He said: “I think that’s what it is. We’d love to be knocking the ball about and score six or seven goals, but sometimes that doesn’t happen.

“Teams come and they sit lower and they make it hard for us.

“At Rangers, that’s going to happen. You need to score goals. I think it’s just that final bit. The final pass, the final shot. I think composure in front of goal. But I can’t complain.

“The boys ran themselves into the ground and I think big Ryan gets his striker’s goal and it’s a massive positive.”

Although he had been pushed into midfield at times in previous games, Penrice started alongside Nico Raskin in the Gers engine room in a tactical move by McInnes which raised some eyebrows.

However, Penrice took it in his stride, saying: “It was obviously not what I’ve been used to in a two. But when the gaffer says play there, there’s no question, I’ll play wherever.

“Whatever I can do to help the team is what I’ll do.

“Obviously, it’s not a position I’ve played in before in the past for Livingstone and Partick.

“But if he asks me to play in there, I’m going to say yes. I could play anywhere.”

#2201. Attenti a dare per morta l’Inter. Roma: che torto a Manchester, ma Gasp lasci stare Baresi. Il vero errore di De Laurentiis: Napoli non è per i grandi gestori. Galliani-Malagò, quanti colpi bassi

La caccia al piccione sull’Inter di Cristian Chivu parte subito. È bastato un derby giocato oggettivamente male per far partire il processo, esterno e in parte interno - perché dei problemi ci sono - a una squadra che in Champions League è tornata a mostrare il suo lato feroce. A Rotterdam, i nerazzurri hanno mandato un messaggio: nonostante i jolly europei siano finiti, ci sono eccome. Quanto al campionato, al termine della scorsa edizione della Serie A l’Inter ha trionfato senza portare a casa quasi nessuno scontro diretto, sicuramente non i derby. Al netto di tutte le incertezze di una squadra che negli ultimi anni ha vinto meno di quello che poteva, e che sicuramente spesso si sopravvaluta rispetto all’avversario, è la continuità il segreto di questa formazione.

Quanto al mercato dei nerazzurri, si fa un gran parlare dell’eventuale quinta punta. Ci divertiamo anche noi, ma intanto Beppe Marotta ha - giustamente - chiuso a Mauro Icardi. E penso che non sia così scontato l’arrivo di un attaccante anche a gennaio. O meglio: avrebbe molto più senso puntare su un ragazzo. Nell’Under 23 forse non ce ne sono di pronti per reggere il ritmo, ma la seconda squadra - in teoria - serve a questo: con un parco attaccanti composto da Lautaro, Thuram, Esposito e Bonny, un ulteriore puntero giocherebbe comunque poco e nulla. Tanto vale dare spazio a un ragazzo che in C ha iniziato a farsi le ossa come, per esempio, Lavelli, già visto.

Tornando alla Champions: a Manchester si è vista una cosa brutta. Non tanto la prestazione sfortunata di Leonardo Balerdi, che pure finora ha fatto benissimo e Gian Piero Gasperini aveva paragonato - per caratteristiche, non valore assoluto - a Franco Baresi. Ecco: lasciamo perdere i paragoni, portano sfiga. La cosa peggiore è quel rigore ribattuto da Bruno Fernandes, per una porzione di spalla di Bryan Cristante in area. Il VAR non è intervenuto per correggere il clamoroso abbaglio dell'arbitro - Cunha cade già prima del presunto contatto con Mancini -, salvo poi consentire ai Red Devils il replay del penalty parato dal portiere giallorosso. E qui c'è bisogno che qualcosa ce la spieghino: o i monitor si accendono sempre o non si accendono mai, così è una sconfitta che lascia un retrogusto amarissimo.

La trasferta del Napoli in casa del Porto sarà lo scenario di un what if per Aurelio De Laurentiis: e se avesse puntato su Francesco Farioli? L’allenatore italiano è un vecchio pallino di ADL, che raramente, quando si è trattato di scegliere il manico, ha sbagliato, ma questa volta sembra di sì. La tentazione è dire che De Laurentiis abbia sbagliato scelta quando è andato sul sicuro: Massimiliano Allegri come Carlo Ancelotti, le due grandi delusioni - posto che poi Carletto s’è preso una rivincita mica da poco su chi pensava fosse finito - dell’era partenopea del produttore cinematografico. A questa impressione si potrebbe però obiettare che, in realtà, anche prendere Antonio Conte, al netto dei dubbi sul rapporto con la piazza (già affrontati però all’Inter), era andare sul sicuro. E che non lo era mica tanto con Rudi Garcia, altro macro errore. Allora, forse, il punto è un altro.

C’entra la squadra: quella attuale ha bisogno di andare a mille all’ora, come faceva con Conte. Con Allegri, che s’è rintanato nella sua immagine di tecnico anti-calcio, questo non succede. C’entra, forse ancora di più, la piazza. Nelle sue meraviglie e contraddizioni, Napoli è la città di Masaniello e mica di Cavour. Napoli, a costo di essere banali, vive di grandi emozioni e non di chi vuole gestire quelle che già ci sono. È un cortocircuito che forse De Laurentiis ha mal considerato, e chissà che quella passione non avrebbe saputo nutrirla meglio lo stesso Farioli o, perché no, quel Vincenzo Italiano su cui, nonostante tanto facesse pensare a lui come uomo giusto, ADL non ha avuto il coraggio di puntare.

È agli sgoccioli la prima fase della lunghissima campagna elettorale tra Adriano Galliani e Giovanni Malagò. Mancano però 40 giorni all’elezione del prossimo presidente federale e saranno molto intensi. Anche nel modo più deteriore del termine, dato che questa partita si gioca anche a base di colpi bassi. Questione di nomine e di ombre (improbabili) di conflitti di potere, doppie firme e un regolamento di conti che rischia di lasciare strascichi pesanti anche quando la FIGC avrà finalmente un nuovo presidente. È una vicenda che, se continuerà su questa falsariga, rischia di spaccare il calcio italiano molto più a lungo di quanto non sembri. E adesso partirà uno squalificante mercatino dei voti. Nel frattempo, di sostanza e contenuti, ci pare ci sia davvero poco, per non dire praticamente nulla. È un gran peccato.

#2200. Allegri a SKY: “Siamo pochi, ci serve una gara di sofferenza. Prendiamo gol facili da evitare”

Massimiliano Allegri, allenatore del Napoli, ha parlato a Sky Sport alla vigilia del match di Champions League contro il Porto: “Infortuni? In allenamento non riusciamo a fare il torello coprendo il cerchio di centrocampo. Dobbiamo preparare la partita, è difficile perché il Porto è un’ottima squadra in casa. Noi dobbiamo fare una gara di sofferenza che credo ci serva anche. Mancano piccoli dettagli per portare a casa i risultati, la dimostrazione è l’alternanza di risultati che stiamo facendo in campionato. In Champions, indipendentemente da questa gara, il destino è nelle nostre mani. Con dieci punti si può andare ai playoff, dovrebbe essere un bel traguardo. In quei momenti ci vuole carattere, voglia di portare a casa il risultato in cui abbiamo lasciato tanti punti e preso tanti gol è una situazione di partita che va migliorata. Bisogno di sofferenza? Ogni tanto soffrendo un po’ serve, prendiamo dei gol troppo facili e questo non va bene, porta all’alternanza dei risultati. Rinforzi a gennaio? Pensare a quello che è successo e quello che sarà servito a poco. Vedremo cosa sarà. L’unica cosa che bisogna fare è andare in campo e giocare bene, la squadra ha fatfo buone partite in alcuni casi. Se prendiamo tutti quei gol negli ultimi trenta minuti vuol dire che non riusciamo a gestire alcuni momenti della partita. Non è questione di assenze, le assenze non sono una giustificazione. Dovrà essere una partita di sofferenza, siamo in tredici. Ci sarà da soffrire con una squadra che sta facendo molto bene. De Bruyne? Non è che non voglio dirlo, ma farà l’allenamento e manderò in campo chi sta in piedi”.

#2199. Veteran with 522 EFL caps backs Lincoln City 23-year-old for ‘a big future’

Lincoln City have fared fairly well in their first 13 games of the 2026/27 Championship season, sitting in 16th with 15 points to their name. The Imps spent on new players like Mikkel Ladefoged and Andrei Coubis in the summer, but among those to impress on the step up from League One has been Deji Elerewe.

Now, the 23-year-old centre-back has received high praise from defensive partner and EFL veteran Sonny Bradley. Speaking to the club’s official media, he said: “I recognised it before the first couple of weeks that he came in the door. I could tell straight away in training that he was a big lad. He was aggressive, he was ready to get stuck in and everything that he was asked to do, he could do comfortably.

“I recognised pretty early that he’s got a big future in the game. He’s had a great start to the season, but it’s just the start. With the mentality that he’s got, I’m pretty sure he’ll want to take it into the rest of this year and certainly into the second half of the season.”

Having made 522 EFL appearances across all three leagues, Sonny Bradley knows what he’s talking about when it comes to impressive young prospects. Lincoln City’s stand-in skipper has played alongside and come up against plenty of top talents across his storied career, so his praise of Elerewe comes as a glowing review.

After starting out at Charlton Athletic, Elerewe made a name for himself at Bromley and earned his move to Sincil Bank in the winter. He started encouragingly, but has really stepped up in the Championship.

Elerewe has played all but six minutes of the Championship campaign so far, locking down a starting spot. He’s among the league’s top 13% of centre-backs for defensive contributions (113) and ranks highly for his interceptions (21 – top 7%), aerial duels won (40 – top 11%) and touches in the opposition box (30 – top 4%).

The Imps ace has the physical stature and power to hold his own against big strikers and he serves as an aerial asset in both boxes. At 23, he is of the age and profile to kick on further and challenge himself at a higher level in the years to come.

Elerewe’s progress at his young age means that excitement over his future is more than justified. He has the physical profile to be a success at all levels, so it will be a case of rounding out his game both defensively and in possession to push to new heights.

Lincoln City will have the firm belief that Elerewe can become a high value asset in the transfer market in the years to come. He has quickly grown into an influential player at Sincil Bank, and that will bring admiring glances from clubs higher up in the food chain.

For now though, Elerewe will be focused on the task at hand with the Imps, where he is under contract until 2029. Alongside his own personal development, the goal for this season is to stay in the Championship, and the London-born defender can have a key part to play in that.

#2197. Celtic Fans Collective demand Dermot Desmond attend AGM in person and face scrutiny

Celtic Fans Collective have called on Dermot Desmond to attend the upcoming Celtic AGM in person.

The supporter group issued a lengthy statement demanding that the Parkhead shareholder show up to the event in person to face scrutiny over boardroom decisions.

The group claims Desmond wields "considerable influence over the direction and decision-making" at the club and must "answer questions about his role".

A Celtic Fans Collective statement read: "For twenty years, Dermot Desmond has not attended Celtic's Annual General Meeting, despite wielding considerable influence over the direction and decision-making of our club.

"Although only a minority shareholder, Desmond appears to exercise influence far beyond his shareholding. With that influence comes a responsibility to be accountable.

"We call on Dermot Desmond to publicly commit to attending the 2026 AGM in person and answer questions about his role in the running of Celtic Football Club.

"Sending his son, another representative or a prepared statement in his place is no substitute for attending personally.

"The decision by Peter Lawwell to prematurely conclude last year's AGM left a clear impression among supporters that the Board had taken an opportunity to avoid scrutiny. Responsibility for how that meeting was conducted and ultimately concluded rests entirely with the Board.

"This year, however, the focus must be firmly on scrutiny rather than protest. There is a clear understanding across the support that the AGM must provide the opportunity for important questions to be put directly to those running the Club, without allowing scrutiny to be evaded once again.

"Celtic supporters have repeatedly sought meaningful dialogue and a more constructive relationship with the Club.

"At a time when fans want to see decisive leadership, a public commitment from Dermot Desmond to attend the AGM in good faith would be an important demonstration of his willingness to engage directly with supporters and shareholders."

Celtic Trust added: "As a Non-Executive Director of the Club, it is the duty of Dermot Desmond to attend the 2026 Celtic PLC AGM.

"He has been absent from these meetings for 20 years - refusing to face and answer questions from shareholders.

"He should commit to ending that absence this year."

#2196. Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

Manchester United (4-2-3-1) Lammens; Mazraoui (Dalot 61), Maguire, Heaven (Martinez 61), Shaw; Tielemans, Santos (Mainoo 61); Diallo (Lacey 61), Fernandes, Dorgu (Rashford 61); Cunha (Mbeumo 61). Subs Zirkzee, Yoro, J Fletcher, T Fletcher, Amass, Collyer, Mee (g), Heath (g), Gabriel. Booked Dorgu.

AC Milan (3-4-2-1) Torriani; Terracciano (Gila 60), Winter (Vladimirov 84), Pavlovic (Diawara 84); Chukwueze, Musah (Ricci 76), Jashari (Modric 60), Estupinan (Bartesaghi 61); Loftus-Cheek (Comotto 84), Cisse (Saelemaekers 60); Ramos (Camarda 75). Subs Pittarella (g), Bouyer (g). Booked Estupinan.

Goals Chukwueze (37), Cisse (57), Ramos (68), Loftus-Cheek (71).

That six-time Champions League winner Luka Modric raised the trophy with the one hand said everything you need to know about this moment...

Aug 30: Manchester United vs Ipswich Town

Sep 13: Manchester United vs Manchester City

United’s pre-season ends in defeat. A wretched second half proves their undoing as Amorim’s Milan score four. Worth reminding that United led this match, twice.

Milan are playing keep-ball in these latter stages and although Mainoo regains possession, his attempt to play forward is cut out and Modric’s outside-of-the-foot pass finds Comotto, who heads straight at Lammens.

Four minutes of added time to be played...

United now raining crosses down on Milan’s box but Torriani equal to it every time.

For the second time this afternoon, Shaw directs a lovely ball into Fernandes’ path in behind Milan’s back line, but the Portugal international can’t bring it under his spell.

Martinez has added a little bit of urgency to United’s build-up. Mbeumo tries to feed Shaw down the line but the ball is cut out.

More substitutions... Diawara, Vladimirov and Comotto enter the field of play in place of Pavlovic, De Winter and Loftus-Cheek.

Big chance for Rashford! Martinez lofts a fantastic ball over the top but Rashford is not quite able to bring it under his spell, with Torriani and De Winter combing to clear their lines.

Milan are now sitting off, settling into a back five as they look to preserve their advantage. Fernandes, Tielemans and Dalot combine well but such has been United’s fortunes this afternoon, the ball ricochets off the referee and play is halted.

Good work from Rashford in the corner to regain possession, but his ball into the box is not picked up by a team-mate.

More changes... Ramos and Musah make way for Camarda and Ricci.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4 (Loftus-Cheek) No sooner had the players returned after the second-half hydration break then Milan exploit United’s exposed left side (again). Ramos sends Loftus-Cheek through and the midfielder composes himself before bending the ball around Lammens.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 3 (Ramos) That’s too easy. United fail to learn their lesson, Shaw not getting tight enough to Chukwueze and the winger’s cross is met by new signing Ramos, who powers a header back across goal and past Lammens.

Loftus-Cheek and Ramos are doing a good job of cutting off the pass into United’s midfield in their build-up phase.

Rashford (who makes his first United appearance in almost two years), Lacey, Dalot, Mbeumo, Mainoo and Martinez replace Dorgu, Amad, Mazraoui, Cunha, Santos and Heaven.

For Milan, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Gila and Modric are on for Cisse, Estupinan, Terracciano and Jashari

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 2 (Cisse) United have set a higher defensive line so far this half, with their front line pressing with more intensity to avoid the ball over the top. However Chukwueze is able to find space around the sides, coming in off the right and curling an effort goalwards which Cisse turns in at the far post. There are calls for offside, but with no VAR here, the goal stands.

Milan win a free-kick some 25 yards out after Fernandes clips Estupinan. Teenager Cisse steps up and fires straight into the United wall. Was always going to be difficult to trouble Lammens from there.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 1 (Dorgu) United wisely decide to keep hold of the ball for a while, the midfield three rotating to disrupt Milan’s out-of-possession shape and open up passing lanes. A Milan throw-in from the right-back berth is precedes an awful backpass by Terracciano which is pounced on by Dorgu who curls the ball beyond Torriani.

United have looked bright in the opening moments of this half. They win a free-kick midway into Milan’s half. The ball is delivered to the back post and, after some 18-yard-box pinball, a relieved Torriano pounces on it.

Both teams remain unchanged as the second 45 minutes begin.

All square at the break. Tough to know what to make of that half – United looked solid enough and could have taken a lead into the interval had Fernandes converted his penalty, but they failed to create a wealth of clear-cut chances. It will be interesting to see how Carrick approaches this second half.

Milan have enjoyed just a tick over two-thirds of possession, which United have contributed to in part through some lackadaisical passing.

Fernandes misses a spot-kick for the second time in two friendlies! Here, Torriani guesses correctly, diving to his right to palm Fernandes’ strike away.

De Winter brings down Tielemans inside the box after Terracciano loses the ball attempting to play out from the back.

Manchester United 1 AC Milan 1 (Chukwueze) It’s all a bit messy. Jashari causes Maguire and Santos to crash into each other (Kaka at Old Trafford, anyone?) off a throw-in, Ramos taking over with the United pair out of commission. He finds Chukwueze who finishes the move off at the far post.

The match becomes stretched momentarily as Pavlovic, the centre-back, marauds forward, setting the ball to Estupinan who delivers another dangerous cross from the left, which Lammens does well to claim.

Santos clips Loftus-Cheek near the byline and the referee awards Milan a free-kick. Chukwueze cuts the ball back to an unmarked Jashari on the edge of the box, but his side-footed effort flies wide.

Milan supporters unfurl a banner paying tribute to the late, great Franco Baresi, who passed away on July 31 aged 66.

Hermosa bandera a Franco Baresi.QUE EN PAZ DESCANSE, LEYENDA DEL FÚTBOL 🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/fvE48nKVSs

United have picked their moments to press. Santos, who has enjoyed a wonderful pre-season, is a little too overzealous in his attempts to regain possession and gives away a foul. But the intent is correct.

Shaw floats a delightful ball over the top for Fernandes to gallop on to. The Portuguese steals in ahead of De Winter but cannot find the target with his weaker left foot.

Cisse escapes the clutches of Mazraoui down the left and fires a shot (more likely a mis-hit cross) straight into the gloves of Lammens.

United finally get their foot on the ball, but Heaven attempts an ambitious cross-field pass and possession goes back to the Italians.

A Mexican wave has already begun. We’re only 21 minutes in...

Carrick’s side continue to sit off, allowing Milan to keep hold of the ball. Cisse works in from the left, playing a neat one-two with Ramos before his curled strike sails well over.

A period of extended possession for Milan, United dropping into a compact 4-4-2 mid-block. Estupinan rains in a dangerous cross from the left and the ball falls to Loftus-Cheek, whose effort is expertly saved by the right boot of Lammens.

Estupinan goes into the book after pulling Amad’s shirt as he looked to dart in behind after Tielemans had played a dangerous through-ball. Might possibly have been the last man?

Tielemans cedes possession to the busy Jashari just outside his own box, the Swiss midfielder moving the ball on to Loftus-Cheek who fires a shot straight at Lammens.

Amad picks Pavlovic’s pocket and the Milan centre-half is forced to concede a corner. United unable to score from this one.

Milan are indeed in Amorim’s preferred 3-4-2-1 formation. They circulate the ball in front of United’s first line of pressure in an attempt to calm things down.

Manchester United 1 AC Milan 0 (Maguire) Fernandes delivers an inswinger from the left and Maguire is there to meet it at the back post, striding past Musa to plant a header past Torriani.

United make a fast start, Dorgu flashing a cross-cum-shot across the face of goal. Torriani gets a fingertip to it and thte ball goes behind for a corner.

Szymon Marciniak, the experienced Polish referee, gets us under way. Milan send the ball back to goalkeeper Torriani.

The players emerge from the tunnel, United debuting their lovely new cream third kit and Milan in their traditional red-and-black home colours. Smoke machines and pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere in Wroclaw...

We are almost ready to go. Let us know your match predictions and thoughts on United’s prospects this season in the comments section beneath this blog.

Manchester United defeated Leeds United on penalties to hoist the mighty Boyle Sports Cup at Croke Park. The match, a 1-1 draw, was brought to an abrupt end after five young pitch invaders ran to the middle of the field to take selfies with Bruno Fernandes. In the shoot-out it was James Justin who missed the “decisive” spot-kick, paving the way for Noussair Mazraoui to win it for United.

Marcus Rashford is on the bench this afternoon and could make his first United appearance since his cameo in a Europa League win over Viktoria Plzen in December 2024. He was frozen out under Amorim and has since been loaned to Aston Villa and Barcelona, but his Old Trafford future under Carrick remains unclear.

Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can push for the Premier League title, but has underlined the urgent need for signings.

The United head coach has taken heart from his squad’s promising preparations for the new campaign and, speaking at their Co Kildare summer base, he explained why he was confident they could build on last season’s third-place finish.

Carrick has been thrilled to hear United’s players discussing what they might achieve and has dared supporters to dream that they can get closer to last year’s champions Arsenal. But he is also a realist and recognises he is not blessed with options.

So far United have added Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, a reserve goalkeeper, but their £83.3m spend is significantly less than what newly promoted clubs Ipswich Town (£109.4m) and Coventry City (£92.2m) have invested in their squads.

Amorim’s side have gone intercontinental this summer, travelling from Scotland to Indonesia, via Australia, before arriving in Poland for the last of their four pre-season games.

In memory of Franco Baresi 🇮🇹♾️ pic.twitter.com/ULAJRjxDvE

Manchester United Lammens; Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw; Tielemans, Santos, Fernandes; Amad, Dorgu; Cunha

Subs Heath, Mee, Amass, Dalot, Martínez, Yoro, Collyer, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Mainoo, Gabriel, Lacey, Mbeumo, Rashford, Zirkzee

AC Milan Torriani; Terracciano, De Winter, Pavlović; Chukwueze, Jashari, Musah, Estupiñán; Loftus-Cheek, Cissè; Ramos

Subs Bouyer, Pittarella, Gila, Diawara, Vladimirov, Ricci, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Modrić, Comotto, Camarda

At his AC Milan unveiling, Amorim was asked about the learnings from his United tenure that he would take into his new role. He said: “The first thing is it’s hard to explain the mistakes because for that I would have to explain the context of the last adventure.

“It’s hard to say to you every mistake. The only thing I can say is that I learned a lot and I made some mistakes.

“I didn’t have the opportunity, and I’m sorry for that, I didn’t have the opportunity to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment and I’m really proud to be their coach for a year in that time.

“But now it’s a different history. There are a lot of things that I could do better in the last experience but sometimes it’s like that, you need to learn to find the right spot to reach a different level and that’s my thinking here.

“Everyone learns from their experience. I learned a lot, I did some mistakes I will try to change, there are some thing you will never change but I think I will be a better manager, that’s all.”

Welcome to live coverage of Manchester United’s final pre-season match, against AC Milan in Wroclaw, Poland. Michael Carrick’s side will look to apply the finishing touches to a promising summer on the pitch, which has included victories over Rosenborg and Atlético Madrid, plus a draw against European champions Paris St-Germain. The team will fly back to Manchester with the big ones, the ones they have always wanted – the Snapdragon Cup and the Boyle Sports Cup – in tow.

At the Tarczynski Stadium there will be a reunion with former manager Ruben Amorim, who was appointed AC Milan’s head coach in June, five months after being sacked by United. Following a frustrating season under Massimiliano Allegri in which Milan fell out of the Champions League spots on the final day, the Rossoneri said Amorim would bring a “modern dominant tactical approach”. His methods failed to cut through at Old Trafford, though, during a tumultuous 14-month reign which finally ended after the Portuguese “blew up” during a heated meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox. At Milan, Amorim has persisted with the 3-4-2-1 formation that was doomed at United.

Carrick made clear this week that United must strengthen if they are to challenge for titles. So far the club have brought in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, but they are still in the market for a left-back and another midfielder. The future of Marcus Rashford has also been a topic of conversation among United fans. The forward has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024 but has joined up with his team-mates in Poland and it remains to be seen if he features in Carrick’s forward planning.

Kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute at this summer’s World Cup, and Lisandro Martínez have also joined up with the team this week and could be handed their first minutes of pre-season having been named in the matchday squad. For Milan, new signing Gonçalo Ramos – bought from PSG for £63m – will make his first appearance in the famous red and black.

#2194. Cardiff City’s injury struggles continue as Brian Barry-Murphy confirms new blow for attacker

Cardiff City face West Ham on Wednesday night, the league’s highest scorers. It marks another tough game in a challenging run of fixtures, and the Bluebirds will be without forward Isaak Davies after a new injury blow.

Brian Barry-Murphy confirmed to BBC Sport Wales that Davies will face four weeks on the sidelines with a hamstring issue. Unfortunately for the City boss, the Welsh attacker is not the only concern, with Perry Ng and Alex Robertson in need of assessment while Dylan Lawlor, Calum Chambers, and Callum Robinson have been out too.

Robinson has been omitted from the last three matchday squads, but the decision has not been expanded on since Barry-Murphy first said ‘certain standards’ had not been met.

Aside from a loan spell in Belgium, Isaak Davies has always played for Cardiff City. He joined the club when he was seven, making his professional debut against Middlesbrough in October 2021 and scoring his first goal against Preston North End in January 2022.

Fans have a natural affection for the player because of his affiliation with the club. However, he has struggled to make a mark on the first team for the most part, and that has continued this term.

Davies has only played 74 minutes of Championship football so far this season, and he is yet to score. His highest goalscoring season for the Bluebirds is six goals, compared to 12 scored in a productive loan spell with KV Kortrijk.

He’s had injury absences to deal with too, impacting his bid to find consistency. It will be hoped this latest blow does not result in an extended spell on the sidelines with four weeks the initial timescale.

Although the news about Davies is a blow, defensive injuries are more of a concern at Cardiff City currently. The Bluebirds will operate with Yousef Salech up front and have the option of Jack Moylan should he be required.

However, defensively, they are without Lawlor, Chambers and Bielik, amongst others. It meant Barry-Murphy had to utilise Joel Colwill and Ollie Tanner as emergency full-backs at the end of the 3-0 defeat to Wolves.

Despite their defensive injuries, City haven’t done too badly at the back in terms of their performances. They have conceded 20 goals, less than nine other teams in the division.

The Bluebirds will be looking to take advantage of their upcoming fixtures, with games against the likes of Norwich City and Preston North End on the horizon. They will be hoping their injury problems ease as soon as possible to give themselves the best possible chance of taking the points in those matches.

#2193. Achraf Hakimi, campione a Parigi. E plusvalenza perfetta per l'Inter di Suning

Giuseppe Marotta aveva portato Achraf Hakimi all'Inter per 40 milioni di euro. Un investimento improvviso e molto importante, in un periodo storico davvero delicato come quello del Covid che, poi, sarà la mazzata sui conti di Suning. Nel giro di appena un anno si è trasformato in una cessione da 67 milioni, garantendo una significativa plusvalenza, ma soprattutto ha permesso al club nerazzurro di far fronte a una situazione economica sempre più complicata. Uno dei momenti più difficili della storia recente dell'Inter, superato anche grazie alle cessioni di Hakimi e Lukaku e al prestito di Oaktree, che ha consentito a Zhang di reperire le risorse necessarie per andare avanti.

Hakimi, nel frattempo, a Parigi ha continuato a fare benissimo. Con la maglia del PSG ha collezionato 220 presenze e 31 gol, compreso quello che ha contribuito a indirizzare la finale di Champions League di Monaco contro la stessa Inter. Oggi è considerato uno dei migliori interpreti del ruolo, oltre a essere uno dei pochi giocatori cresciuti nel Real Madrid e poi lasciati partire senza avere davvero l'opportunità di affermarsi con la prima squadra.

La stagioni culminate con le vittorie della Champions League con il Paris Saint-Germain lo hanno portato anche tra i possibili candidati al Pallone d'Oro. Oggi Achraf Hakimi compie 28 anni.

#2192. Under-fire figure eyed Leicester City boss Russell Martin for top Premier League job in 2024

Leicester City hired Russell Martin in the summer, bringing him in to lead their rebuild after relegation from the Championship. The LCFC boss has faced criticism for inconsistent performances and a frustrating style of play, but it wasn’t long ago that he was held in very high regard.

Martin’s work at MK Dons, Swansea City and in winning promotion to the Premier League with Southampton saw him build a strong reputation in the game. So much so, Manchester United sporting director Jason Wilcox – who worked with Martin at St. Mary’s – put him forward as a candidate to monitor when the Red Devils were considering their Erik ten Hag replacements in 2024.

Wilcox viewed Martin as someone to monitor and consider for the role in the future, rather than as an immediate option. This was shortly before the 2024 FA Cup final in May, so around the same time as the Championship play-off final, which the Saints won.

Wilcox moved from Manchester City to Southampton in 2023, stepping into a director of football role for the first time. He would hire Martin from Swansea City shortly after, and the two found success together.

With Martin as manager and Wilcox as a director, the Saints would win immediate promotion back to the Premier League. It saw the stocks of both surge, but the boss stayed put while Wilcox was tempted away to become technical director in a new-look Manchester United hierarchy, before seeing his title switched to director of football.

Neither have found the same fortunes since though. Martin was eventually sacked by Southampton as they sat bottom of the Premier League table, and a dismal 17-game spell at Rangers led to his next managerial opportunity coming in League One with Leicester City.

Wilcox meanwhile remains at Manchester United, but he has been under-fire for shortcomings in recruitment. Many supporters pin their continued struggles on him, and he was in the line of fire when defender Lisandro Martinez called out the club hierarchy too.

Managerial stock comes and goes, and few have experienced the highs and lows quite like Martin. His work in rebuilding Southampton and getting them promoted earned rave reviews, and rightly so.

However, he stuck by his playing principles on the step up to the Premier League, and it backfired badly. Some would argue he has never really recovered from that, with criticisms over his playing style following him to Rangers and Leicester City, and his willingness to speak up and stick to his guns while speaking to the press brings ridicule.

Despite this, he is still a young manager at only 40, and his CV shows how he can rebuild struggling clubs and build a philosophy for fans, players and staff alike to buy into.

Martin is trying to replicate his past success at Leicester City. He faces an uphill battle to do so, but that will not deter him as both he and LCFC fight to return to their previous heights.

#2190. The curious case of Joe Aribo as Rangers hero triggers comeback from football exile

Former Rangers hero Joe Aribo has been without a club since leaving Southampton in the summer following a loan spell at Leicester City.

It's a curious case for the former Ibrox maverick. Devastatingly effective on his day, yet clubless at the age of 30.

But Aribo is doing the opposite of giving in. He is currently putting in the hard yards in Dubai as he aims to reignite his career.

The midfielder's versatility was one of his greatest strengths, as he demonstrated by starting and scoring in the Europa League Final against Eintracht Frankfurt in Seville while operating as a makeshift false nine.

Aribo thrilled supporters during his time in Glasgow and went on to become an important player for Southampton, making 111 appearances for the Saints and sampling life in the Premier League.

Steven Gerrard adored him and Giovanni van Bronckhorst could scarcely do without him.

Now, however, Aribo finds himself on the outside looking in after the most frustrating period of his career.

Read more: Celtic supporter group demand Dermot Desmond end 20-year absence and attend AGM

Game time proved hard to come by at Southampton under Tonda Eckert and an ill-fated loan move to Leicester did little to improve matters. Minutes were scarce at the King Power and relegation only added to the disappointment.

For a player who once dazzled on European nights and played a leading role in one of Rangers' greatest modern runs, it has been a sobering fall from grace.

But the Nigeria international is now rested, recharged and desperate for another opportunity to prove he can still perform at the highest level.

The hard work is being done behind the scenes. Now Aribo is simply waiting on the chance to remind everyone why he was once one of the most coveted talents in Scottish football.

#2188. West Brom begin talks over new contract for £1.5m star

West Brom named George Campbell as their new club captain in the summer following a stellar debut campaign from the American defender. Signed for £1.5m from CF Montreal in 2025, he has emerged as a key player for WBA.

Now, the Baggies are looking to reward Campbell’s success with a new contract. Reporter Mike McGrath says on X that the club are in talks over a fresh deal for the 25-year-old, despite the fact he is already tied down until 2029 as it stands.

Prior to the summer transfer window, reports stated that Campbell had interest from Scottish giants Celtic, amongst other clubs. A new contract would further secure the American international’s future at The Hawthorns in case admiration from elsewhere grows.

Campbell had impressed in the MLS with CF Montreal after coming through the Atlanta United academy. He has made the step up to Championship football brilliantly, swiftly locking down a starting spot last term and growing in influence over time.

The Pennsylvania native spent the early days of his West Brom career playing at right-back, but shortly after his caretaker appointment, James Morrison moved Campbell into his regular central role and it brought instant results. In the final 11 games of last season, Campbell started all at centre-back and WBA were beaten just once, keeping seven clean sheets along the way.

The American provided some key attacking contributions too, scoring the Baggies’ only goals in draws against Charlton Athletic and Sheffield United, and in a win over Bristol City.

Campbell’s emergence as a key player saw his leadership traits shine through, earning him the captaincy in the summer. He has retained a big role in Albion’s success this term, contributing to the joint-tightest defence in the league with 13 goals conceded while ranking highly for successful passes (694 – top 5% of Championship centre-backs) and successful dribbles (eight – top 3%).

A new Campbell contract isn’t a must because of the time remaining on his existing deal. However, it will play a big part in keeping him happy and fending off potential admirers.

Improved terms reflect his value in the side as West Brom captain and a standout centre-back. It means that any potential admirers will have to part with a pretty penny to try and tempt him away from The Hawthorns.

His club success has brought more opportunities on the international stage, starting in two USMNT fixtures over the last break. As Campbell’s stock grows, WBA know they have to keep him happy if he’s to stay for the foreseeable.

#2186. Hibs' astonishing 47-year Hampden record vs Rangers sets up classic

Hibernian head into next month's Premier Sports Cup Final against Rangers with their tails up.

Granted the club's Scottish Premiership form leaves plenty to be desired, but their semi-final victory over fierce rivals Hearts on Sunday afternoon highlighted the fighting spirit still within the camp.

Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath's goals cancelled out Claudio Braga's early opener and set up the showpiece finale at Hampden Park on December 13. And it turns out Hibs have more to be excited and confident about given their history against the Light Blues at the national stadium.

Marink Reedijk's squad will square off against Derek McInnes' charges and they will do so with the bit between their teeth in the competition. But they also have history on their side.

Hibs have astonishingly not been beaten by Rangers at Hampden in a whopping 47 years.

The last time the Glasgow outfit came out on top was at the 1979 Scottish Cup final which took three attempts following a goalless draw in the initial final and then another in the replay. Rangers would win the third contest 3-2.

Since that period the two clubs have faced off four more times at Hampden and the Leith side have come out on top each time.

First came in the League Cup semi-final of 1991 when Keith Wright netted the winner inside the first 30 minutes. Then in 2004 Hibs progressed to the final of the same competition with a penalty shootout victory over their opponents following a 1-1 draw after extra-time. Stephen Dobbie had levelled after Michael Mols had opened the scoring for Gers during normal time.

The iconic 2016 Scottish Cup Final was next when former defender and then head coach David Gray bulleted home the winning header after an exhausting 3-2 victory for Hibs.

And in 2021 Hibs continued their reign of Hampden dominance over Rangers when they knocked them out of the League Cup at the semi-final stage again. Boyle fired in a stunning first-half hattrick before Scott Arfield nicked a consolation.

It's a staggering statistic and one Hibs will be desperate to add to when the final rolls around next month.
